content.text:
All tests pass. Here is a summary of the change:

**CVE-2026-15920 backport to Django 4.2:** `display_for_field()` in `django/contrib/admin/utils.py` previously had no special handling for `URLField` values, so they fell through to `display_for_value()` and were rendered as plain text (the 5.x branch that rendered them as links didn't exist in 4.2). The fix adds an explicit `URLField` branch that first runs `URLValidator` against the stored value; if validation passes (i.e., the scheme is `http://` or `https://`), the value is rendered as a clickable `<a>` link — matching the safe rendering behaviour introduced upstream. If validation fails (e.g., a `javascript:` or other dangerous scheme), `display_for_value()` is called instead, emitting plain escaped text. The two new imports (`ValidationError` from `django.core.exceptions` and `URLValidator` from `django.core.validators`) are the only other changes.
